offence_severity: Minimum 10 years rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.10,000/-, in default further one year rigorous imprisonment
physical_harm: Severe burn injuries leading to death
premeditation_planning: The court found premeditation/planning as the appellant instigated the deceased to commit suicide
motive: Demand for money from the deceased's father and illicit relationship with the second accused
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the consistent statements of PWs 3, 9, and 11, the recoveries made at the place of occurrence (kerosene cane, piece of cloth soaked in kerosene, quilt and pillows, clothes worn by the deceased with kerosene smell), the postmortem report, and the evidence of the postmortem doctor P.W.15.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that their consistent statements about the appellant's conduct and the deceased's grievances were supported by evidence and that there was no indication of ulterior motives.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 26.05.1987; Trial judgment: 24.12.2008; High Court decision: Not stated; Supreme Court decision: September 4, 2012
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Ravi Kumar Tomar, Amitava Acharjee, H.B. Tiwari, Smriti; Counsel for the State: Chanchal Kumar Ganguly, Avijit Bhattacharjee
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Acquittal; High Court: Conviction on both charges; Supreme Court: Dismissed the appeal
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellant instigated the deceased to commit suicide by pouring kerosene on herself and setting herself on fire, and that the deceased's suicide was a result of the appellant's cruelty, including demanding money from her father and his illicit relationship with his niece.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the deceased's suicide was not instigated by the appellant, and that the prosecution's case was based on circumstantial evidence without establishing the necessary ingredients for the offences under Sections 306 and 498A of the IPC.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied Section 113A of the Evidence Act, which allows a presumption of abetment of suicide if the deceased committed suicide within seven years of marriage and was subjected to cruelty by the husband or his relatives.
precedent_relied_upon: Ramesh Kumar v. State of Chhattisgarh (2001) 9 SCC 618; Thanu Ram v. State of Madhya Pradesh (Now Chhattisgarh) (2010) 10 SCC 353; K. Prema S. Rao and Anr. v. Yadla Srinivasa Rao and Ors. (2003) 1 SCC 217; Devi Lal v. State of Rajasthan (2007) 14 SCC 176
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the High Court found the appellant guilty of abetment under Section 306 and cruelty under Section 498A of the IPC, based on the evidence that the deceased's suicide was instigated by the appellant.
other_sentence_order: The appellant was sentenced to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs.10,000/-, in default to suffer further one year rigorous imprisonment for the offence under Section 306 of IPC. He was also sentenced to suffer rigorous imprisonment for three years apart from a fine of Rs.10,000/-, in default to suffer further rigorous imprisonment for one year for the offence under Section 498A of IPC. Both sentences were directed to run consecutively.
